quests.question: Either the caretaker or the assistant ___ responsible for locking up.
quests.hint: With 'either...or', check the noun that's closest to the blank.
quests.explanation: In 'either...or' sentences, the verb agrees with the noun nearest to it - here, 'the assistant', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Either my brother or my sister ___ picking me up from the airport.
quests.hint: Look at the second name in the pair, not the first, to decide the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'my sister', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Either the printer or the scanner ___ broken.
quests.hint: The noun right before the verb is what matters in an 'either...or' sentence.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the scanner', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Either the manager or the employees ___ responsible for this decision.
quests.hint: This time, the second option is plural - see how that changes the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the employees', which is plural, so the verb is 'are', even though 'the manager' (singular) comes first.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number

quests.question: Either the students or the teacher ___ mistaken about the schedule.
quests.hint: Compare this to the last question - here the second option is singular instead.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the teacher', which is singular, so the verb is 'is', even though 'the students' (plural) comes first.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number

quests.question: Either the coaches or the player ___ going to speak to the press.
quests.hint: Focus on 'the player', not 'the coaches', since it's the noun right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the player', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb, even when the two nouns differ in number

quests.question: Neither the coach nor the players ___ happy with the result.
quests.hint: Just like 'either...or', 'neither...nor' agrees with the noun right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the players', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the players nor the coach ___ happy with the result.
quests.hint: Notice the order has been reversed from the last question - check how that changes the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is now 'the coach', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the parents nor the child ___ aware of the mistake.
quests.hint: Check the second noun in the pair, since it's the one right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the child', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the president nor the board members ___ available for comment.
quests.hint: The second noun here is plural - let that decide the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the board members', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the recipe nor the ingredients ___ easy to find.
quests.hint: 'Ingredients' is right before the verb - match the verb to that.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the ingredients', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready for the fire drill.
quests.hint: 'Students' comes right before the verb here - use that to decide the agreement.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the students', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Not only the owner but also the employees ___ invited to the celebration.
quests.hint: 'Not only...but also' behaves just like 'either...or' - check the noun closest to the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the employees', which is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Not only...but also' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Not only the players but also the coach ___ frustrated with the loss.
quests.hint: This time, the noun right before the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the coach', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Not only...but also' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Not only the recipe but also the cooking method ___ important for this dish.
quests.hint: Check the second item in the pair, since it's the one right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the cooking method', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Not only...but also' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: The editor, as well as her assistants, ___ attending the conference.
quests.hint: 'As well as' just adds extra information - it doesn't create a true compound subject like 'and' does.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the editor', which is singular; 'as well as her assistants' is just added detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The students, as well as their teacher, ___ excited about the field trip.
quests.hint: The phrase after 'as well as' doesn't change how many students there are.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the students', which is plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: This recipe, as well as several others in the book, ___ easy to follow.
quests.hint: Focus on the original subject before the comma, not the phrase after 'as well as'.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'this recipe', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The CEO, together with several board members, ___ reviewing the proposal.
quests.hint: 'Together with' works just like 'as well as' - it doesn't add a second subject.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the CEO', which is singular; 'together with several board members' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The players, along with their coach, ___ heading to the airport tonight.
quests.hint: 'Along with' behaves the same way - check the original subject before the comma.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the players', which is plural. The verb is 'are'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: This document, together with several attachments, ___ ready to be sent.
quests.hint: The attachments mentioned after 'together with' don't change the number of the main subject.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'this document', which is singular. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The bride, accompanied by her parents, ___ into the ceremony hall.
quests.hint: 'Accompanied by' introduces extra detail, just like 'as well as' and 'together with'.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the bride', which is singular; 'accompanied by her parents' is extra detail. The verb takes -s: 'walks'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The whole family, including the grandparents, ___ attending the reunion this year.
quests.hint: 'Including' works the same way - the original subject decides the verb.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the whole family', a singular collective noun; 'including the grandparents' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: The tour group, accompanied by two guides, ___ the museum every Tuesday.
quests.hint: The guides mentioned after 'accompanied by' don't change the number of the main subject.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the tour group', which is singular. The verb takes -s: 'visits'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Accompanied by' / 'including' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Either the volunteers or the coordinator ___ responsible for setting up the event.
quests.hint: This sentence uses 'either...or' - remember, the noun closest to the verb decides.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the coordinator', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: The coordinator, as well as the volunteers, ___ responsible for setting up the event.
quests.hint: This sentence uses 'as well as' instead - the rule is different here. Check the original subject, not the nearest noun.
quests.explanation: Unlike 'either...or', 'as well as' doesn't shift agreement to the nearest noun. The original subject is 'the coordinator', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'As well as' does not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Neither the interns nor the manager ___ aware of the schedule change.
quests.hint: This sentence uses 'neither...nor' - apply the proximity rule one more time.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the manager', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: Either the actors or the director ___ making the final decision on this scene.
quests.hint: Bring back the 'either...or' rule: check the noun right before the verb.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the director', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Either...or' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb

quests.question: The director, along with the actors, ___ making the final decision on this scene.
quests.hint: This sentence uses 'along with' - remember, that phrase doesn't shift the agreement.
quests.explanation: The original subject is 'the director', which is singular; 'along with the actors' is extra detail. The verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Together with' / 'along with' do not change the number of the original subject

quests.question: Neither the reviewers nor the editor ___ satisfied with the final draft.
quests.hint: As a final check, apply the 'neither...nor' proximity rule one more time.
quests.explanation: The noun closer to the verb is 'the editor', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.grammarRule: 'Neither...nor' agreement follows the noun closer to the verb
